data.cultural_impact: The name Sheba became known in the wider culture because of the biblical mention of the queen Sheba, who is believed to have been the Queen of Sheba, a kingdom in southern Arabia or Ethiopia in ancient times. Her visit to King Solomon's court is recorded in the books of I Kings and II Chronicles, and her story has been the subject of countless works of art, literature, and films. The name Sheba has been used as a given name for girls since ancient times and has been popular in various cultures, including the Middle East, Europe, and the Americas.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Bible, the name Sheba is associated with the idea of an oath or a promise, as it is derived from the Hebrew word for 'seven', which is believed to represent completeness or perfection. In this context, the name Sheba can be seen as a symbol of commitment and faithfulness, as she is described in the Bible as having made a long journey to fulfill her promise to visit King Solomon. The name Sheba can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of keeping one's promises and remaining faithful to one's commitments, whether they be to God or to others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sheba, the Queen of Sheba, is mentioned in the Bible in 1 Kings 10:1-13 and 2 Chronicles 9:1-12. The name Sheba carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
